spec.title: Clean up repository responsibilities while preserving behavior
spec.boundary: Existing application, transport, persistence, deterministic-policy, and resource-lifetime boundaries across the repository. Use concrete functions and existing repositories; introduce no general workflow framework, new dependency, schema change, endpoint, provider policy, or scoring rule.
spec.problem: The reports establish mixed serving/generation lifecycles, transaction-sensitive application logic embedded in routes and coordinators, shared policies owned by consumers, repeated persistence and resource-wiring mappings, diagnostic strings used as calculation inputs, and narrow gaps in core regression coverage. These require synchronized maintenance across responsibilities that already have meaningful separation points.
spec.change: Execute one repository cleanup in the following priority order after the test-freeze prerequisite. (1) Generation lifecycle split: move Serving, GenerationUnavailable and serve_next into problems/serving.py; put the shared eligibility functions, capability check and MAX_CLAIMS in problems/eligibility.py. Keep generation execution and run_for_user in runs.py. Update production consumers and retain compatibility exports from runs.py, including historical CHUNK_LIMIT and _query imports. Generation retry decomposition: extract the per-statement answer-key-and-gate cycle from _run_generation, returning explicit attempt, failure, completion and control-flow results to the outer coordinator; keep preparation, plan traversal and run-wide accumulation there. Generation outcome mapping: introduce one noncommitting record_generation_outcome function in runs.py and use it from run_for_user, the problem CLI and the comparison collector, retaining the collector's record_generation entry point. (2) Shared problem access: move served_to intact into problems/access.py and route all consumers to that implementation; preserve the submissions.served_to binding used by hint-timing tests. (3) Comparison job decomposition: extract learner setup and outcome projection into local collection helpers while collect_job retains its explicit commit, preparing flag, exception scopes and publication sequence. Reading-contract ownership: move _reading, validate_reading, validate_supplement, _quoted, validate_diagnostics and their policy constants into ops/creativity_reading.py, which imports no reader, report, evaluation or evidence command module; retain old imported names. SDK transport duplication: move only the repeated original-client/replacement-client installation mechanism into ops/creativity_transport.py. Existing callers still construct the adapter and HTTP context, start their timers, own their try/finally blocks and close the adapter. Do not edit llm/adapter.py. (4) Rating attempt storage: move the three scoped history queries and replay-snapshot update into methods on the existing AttemptRepository; retain scoring decisions, conditional invocation and locks in rating_update.py. (5) Hint lifecycle: extract a concrete service into hints.py for eligibility, reuse, generation and durable recording; keep HTTP error mapping and citation response construction in api/problems.py. Explanation preparation: move only the fresh eligibility and target-context block into explanation.py, returning eligible analysis/context or no result. (6) History replay: separate loading, ordinary/placement transitions and result assembly within profile_read.py, sharing the existing rating arithmetic. Field-progress assembly: move domain assembly into profile_read.py; retain api.profile._fields as the response-conversion seam and retain its observable placement binding for frozen tests. (7) Archive metadata: extract metadata derivation from artifacts into functions consuming already-loaded source/context data. Exact export boundary: add exact-revision lookup to EvidenceRepository and split export_evidence into ordered preparation and writing, with every entry prepared before the first write. (8) Wiki label dispatch: move the four label handlers and resolve_author to wiki/label_commands.py, keeping parser/resource ownership and compatibility entry points in wiki/__main__.py. Written-draft persistence: replace the two _generate/_extract persistence blocks with one local helper preserving provenance, commit and pre-settlement ID capture. (9) English rewrite decomposition: extract packet validation, placement-binding calculation and postcondition checking inside english.py; keep locks, mutation, savepoint and report publication in apply_english_rewrite. (10) Reference construction: extract source-evidence preparation and provisional-label comparison inside reference_staging.py while construct retains stage changes, error conversion, rollback and checkpointing. Leave the duplicated report calculations unchanged because reference_bundles.py is fingerprint-bound. (11) Placement Item duplication: share common Item assembly while callers retain their different early-stop, saved-band and closure behavior. Prerequisite calculation: keep _standing_before's loading wrapper and extract its observation, ancestry, traversal and route calculation over loaded inputs. (12) Shadow lifecycle: extract claim/reservation and settlement operations inside shadow.py; process_one retains provider execution between the two transactions. (13) Profile creation: move uniqueness policy and atomic profile/enrolment creation into profile_creation.py; return domain values and explicit domain refusals, with HTTP mapping and serialization retained in api/profile.py. (14) Authentication lifecycle: extract a local authentication hook in page.tsx at the existing verification-effect position; retain session subscription wiring and profile resets in Page so effect registration and callback sequencing remain unchanged. Workspace request duplication: consolidate the three concrete progress request chains locally while each caller retains its trigger and result-application guard. (15) Translation text processing: extract deterministic masking/preparation and validation/restoration functions within translation.py, leaving cache/provider orchestration in TranslationOverlay.text. (16) Host utility ownership: move command, checksum and backup_lock unchanged to ops/host.py; update all nine comparison modules and retain ops.backup compatibility imports plus direct-script execution support. Backup coverage: add restore validation, recovery-container cleanup and successful-publication tests without restructuring backup orchestration. (17) Skeleton structural facts: expose explicit structural-check facts from skeleton.py and render the existing scaffold_refusals list from them; change best_plan to consume facts instead of diagnostic wording, list slicing or count-minus-one. Coordinate duplication: share the existing UTF-8 AST byte-to-character conversion with cut_count. Skeleton coverage: add real multi-block search, witness-ranking and multibyte-counting regressions before this split. (18) Yield reporting: move the complete calculation/rendering bundle into problems/yield_report.py and retain command-module compatibility exports. (19) Worker accounting: introduce one lifespan-local helper that starts and registers an already-constructed thread, preserving increment-before-start and BaseException rollback. (20) Semantic CLI coverage: add offline protocol-drift and actual-model-version-drift rejection tests while leaving semantic_evaluation.py byte-identical. Remove only imports and duplicated implementation blocks rendered unused by these named extractions; retain required compatibility names.
spec.impact: This is the single preserve unit across all affected pipelines. Shared access, eligibility, outcome recording, repositories and host utilities move with their consumers and compatibility exports. There is no required behavior-changing prerequisite for the included work. Evaluator decomposition, reference report deduplication and diagnostic helper relocation instead depend on a future simplify contract decision or explicit rework contract_change for frozen evidence compatibility; they are not folded into this spec. Existing authoring-policy violations require separate behavior work. New source provenance will honestly identify the refactored code: existing source-drift refusals, preparation requirements and historical evidence remain intact. New paid collection is not authorized by this cleanup.
spec.rollback: Revert the production extractions and consumer-import changes together, restoring the original implementations and removing the newly introduced production modules. No schema or data migration is involved. The characterization additions can remain because they must pass against the pre-refactor implementation. Never roll back by rewriting archived evidence, changing policy hashes or deleting durable experiment records.

spec.title: Separate repository responsibilities while preserving observable behavior
spec.boundary: Existing pipeline responsibilities and their shared adapters. Extract implementations into their existing owning domains; preserve public entry points and compatibility delegates. Keep transport, policy, transaction, resource, and rendering responsibilities distinct without changing their contracts.
spec.problem: The reports confirm shared request decoding in a browser executor; distributed speech-mode selection and duplicated publisher mechanics; transport-owned resource lifecycles; authentication and authoring lifecycles embedded in large browser components; duplicated validation, persistence, and serialization rules; and policy/report construction embedded in orchestration. These force unrelated changes through the same implementation boundaries. The evidence supports structural extraction, not behavior repair or a measured performance claim.
spec.change: First read the existing regression bodies for every named debt and reconcile the reported baseline failures. Add the narrowly scoped tests listed below against the original entry points, record their baseline results, and freeze all new test bodies and expectations before moving production code. Existing test files remain untouched. Add React 18-compatible react-test-renderer and its types as test-only frontend dependencies, updating the lockfile, to exercise current component callbacks without changing the Vitest configuration. Then execute the following responsibility extractions in qualitative payoff order. (1) request-option-decoding: move the five public decoders, their two private helpers, and two constant tables into api/request_options.py; update the three route consumers at their existing call positions and retain compatibility exports from browser_turn_execution.py. spec.title: Serialize index batches with generation replacement
spec.boundary: Generation selection, binding cleanup, outbox completion, and rebuild activation.
spec.problem: Worker batches retain a generation independently of rebuild activation. An old-generation batch can delete newly active bindings and complete its task without restoring the active index.
spec.change: Introduce one repository-owned generation-write coordination scope used by worker batches and rebuild. Use a PostgreSQL advisory lock held by a dedicated connection so separate service instances share the boundary; release it in finally and on connection loss. A batch acquires it before choosing a generation or claiming tasks and retains it through binding changes and completion. Rebuild acquires it before enumerating authoritative documents and retains it through verification and activation or failure. Keep arriving authoritative mutations in the existing outbox for processing against the active generation after release. Preserve the existing nonblocking duplicate-rebuild rejection. Do not hold a long authoritative-data transaction across model work.
